parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A satellite of mass $m$ has a circular orbit of radius $r$ about a planet of mass $M$. It may be assumed that the planet and the satellite are uniform spheres that are isolated in space.

Show that the linear speed $v$ of the satellite is given by the expression

$$v = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$$

where $G$ is the gravitational constant.
Explain your working.

parts.text:
The planet spins about its own axis with angular speed $1.7 \times 10^{-4} \text{rad s}^{-1}$. Moon A is always above the same point on the planet's surface.
